previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a flare of chronic pancreatitis, presenting with severe abdominal pain, nausea, and inability to tolerate oral intake. She was managed with her established IV pain and nausea regimen, kept NPO initially, and gradually advanced to full oral intake and J tube use by day six. On hospital day four, she developed fever and erythema at her peripheral IV site, diagnosed as thrombophlebitis; IV vancomycin was given briefly but discontinued after resolution and negative blood cultures. Imaging revealed a chronic thrombosis in the right internal jugular vein. Warfarin was held on admission due to supratherapeutic INR and poor intake, with enoxaparin bridging initiated once INR was subtherapeutic. Hypertension was managed with IV metoprolol as needed, and lisinopril was restarted at discharge. Depression and anxiety were addressed with reinstitution of amitriptyline and a short course of Ativan. A port placement was arranged outpatient for future access. She improved clinically and was discharged home on her baseline medications, enoxaparin, and instructions to monitor INR.
problems: Phlebitis and thrombophlebitis of other sites
Acute venous embolism and thrombosis of internal jugular veins
Acute upper respiratory infections of unspecified site

radiology_notes.text:
PICC LINE PLACEMENT

INDICATION: IV access needed for antibiotics.

The procedure was explained to the patient. A timeout was performed.

RADIOLOGIST: Dr. ___, Dr. ___ and Dr. ___ performed
the procedure.  The attending Dr. ___ was present and supervising during the
entire procedure.

TECHNIQUE: Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right brachial
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after
establishing intravenous access are on file. A peel-away sheath was then
placed over a guidewire and a double lumen PICC line measuring 42.5 cm in
length was then placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in
the SVC under fluoroscopic guidance. Position of the catheter was confirmed by
a fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed. The catheter was secured
to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION: Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided 5 ___
double-lumen PICC line placement via the right brachial venous approach. Final
internal length is 42.5 cm, with the tip positioned in SVC. The line is ready
to use.
